title: Integrated Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition Playbook
author: Sophie Martinez
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's end-to-end processes and controls for budgeting & forecasting, contract review & approval, procurement procedures, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, Product, and Engineering stakeholders involved in commercial commitments, purchasing, and accounting close activities. Follow the procedures below to ensure consistent approvals, timely recognition, and audit-ready documentation.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood entities and product lines (Redwood Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Console, Redwood Optimize).
- Covers OPEX and CAPEX procurement, third-party contracts, customer contracts, subscription and usage billing, and month/quarter/year financial close activities.

Roles & ownership:
- Finance (FP&A & Revenue Accounting): lead forecasting cadence, prepare forecasts, implement revenue recognition, manage invoicing and collections.
- Legal: contract review, risk assessment, required clause approvals (IP, data protection, liability).
- Procurement: vendor onboarding, PO issuance, vendor terms negotiation within delegated authority.
- Product/Eng & Sales: provide contract requirements, expected delivery dates, usage estimates, and technical acceptance criteria.
- Approvals matrix owner: VP Finance (maintains approval thresholds and delegation).

1) Budgeting & Forecasting (cadence & artifacts)
- Cadence:
  1. Annual operating budget (AOB) prepared in Sep-Nov for next FY; leadership review in Dec; board submission in Jan.
  2. Quarterly reforecast (rolling 12 months) carried out at the end of each quarter.
  3. Monthly variance analysis published with actuals within 8 business days of month-end.
- Artifacts and models:
  - Master GL-backed budget workbook (single source of truth).
  - Product-level P&L templates (Hosted / Dedicated / Private / Optimize).
  - Headcount and hiring plan (HC tracker integrated with HR system).
- Forecast rules and tolerances:
  - Revenue: use closed-won ARR + expected renewals + usage estimates; growth variances >10% require leadership sign-off.
  - OPEX: rolling forecast should flag variances >5% for director-level review; >10% requires VP Finance action plan.
  - Capital requests: CAPEX > $50k require CFO approval and business case.

2) Contracting & Legal process (customer & vendor)
- Standard contract types: MSA, SaaS Order Form, Professional Services SOW, Vendor Master Agreement, NDA.
- Contract intake:
  1. Sales or Procurement submits contract via Contract Intake form (Confluence link) and uploads to Contract Management System (DocuSign/CLM).
  2. Legal triages within 2 business days; high-value or non-standard terms flagged for priority review.
- Approval matrix (customer-facing, simplified):
  | Contract Value | Legal Review | Finance Approval | Executive Approval |
  |----------------|--------------|------------------|--------------------|
  | <$25k          | Standard T&Cs | Sales Manager     | Not required       |
  | $25k-$250k     | Legal (standard) | Finance Director | CRO / VP Finance   |
  | >$250k         | Legal (senior) | VP Finance       | CEO & GC review     |
- Mandatory contract clauses and redlines checklist:
  - Data protection & processing (DPA), data residency if requested.
  - Liability cap: default is 3x fees, deviations require GC approval.
  - IP and ownership: standard Redwood ownership of model code; customer data belongs to customer.
  - Audit & SOC access: include where required by enterprise deals.
  - Payment terms: standard Net30; deviations must be approved by Finance.
- Contract storage and metadata:
  - All fully executed contracts must be stored in CLM with metadata fields: counterparty, effective date, term, auto-renew, revenue account, contact, contract owner.

3) Procurement procedures (vendor onboarding & PO flow)
- Vendor classification: Strategic, Standard, One-off. Strategic vendors require SOW, security review, and exec sponsorship.
- Request and approval thresholds:
  - <$10k: Dept manager approval; Procurement issues PO.
  - $10k-$100k: Department head + Procurement review; requires vendor W-9/SOW/insurance.
  - >$100k: Procurement + VP Finance + Legal + competitive sourcing (if recurring) and CFO sign-off.
- Procurement steps (numbered):
  1. Requestor completes Procurement Request form with business justification, GL code, and expected delivery date.
  2. Procurement validates vendor, tax forms, and security posture (if required).
  3. Legal reviews contract template for non-standard terms.
  4. Procurement issues PO or signs vendor agreement per delegation; returns executed copy to requester and Finance.
  5. AP matches invoice to PO and goods/service acceptance before payment.
- Vendor onboarding checklist:
  - Signed vendor agreement or PO, W-9/Tax ID, insurance certificate (if required), security questionnaire (for vendors accessing data), banking/payment details, vendor contact.

4) Revenue recognition & billing policies (summary & examples)
- Accounting standard: ASC 606 (IFRS 15 principles) applied consistently across product lines.
- Core policy rules (plain language):
  1. Identify the contract and performance obligations.
  2. Determine the transaction price (subscription fees, usage, one-time setup).
  3. Allocate the transaction price to performance obligations.
  4. Recognize revenue when obligations are satisfied: over time (ratably) or at a point in time.
- Product-specific guidance:
  - Subscription (monthly/annual): recognized ratably over the subscription term. Annual prepay: recognized monthly over the 12-month service term.
  - Usage-based billing (API tokens / embedding units): recognized when usage occurs (measured each billing period) or upon invoicing if immaterial timing difference.
  - Professional services / implementation: recognize over time if customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefit; otherwise at completion and acceptance.
  - Upfront non-refundable setup fees: amortize over the expected contractual period unless a separate performance obligation is identified.
- Billing terms and invoicing:
  - Default payment terms: Net30 from invoice date. Exceptions (Net45/Net60) require VP Finance approval.
  - Currency & tax handling: Invoice in customer-preferred currency if supported; VAT/GST applied per customer jurisdiction; Sales Tax team to validate nexus.
  - Late payments: 1.5% monthly interest after 30 days default and escalation to Sales Ops for collections.
- Deferred revenue & cutoffs:
  - Close checklist: revenue cut-off review performed monthly by Revenue Accounting; deferred revenue schedules must be reconciled each close with supporting contracts and invoices.

5) Controls, reporting, and audit readiness
- Required artifacts for audit: executed contracts, signed SOWs, approved POs, invoices, receipts, GL entries, revenue deferral schedules, and forecast backup.
- Segregation of duties: Procurement cannot approve its own invoices for payment; approvers must be independent of requestors.
- Exception handling: Material deviations (approval threshold bypass, unusual payment terms) require an exception memo and CFO sign-off.
- KPIs and monitoring:
  - Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) target: <45 days.
  - Forecast accuracy: revenue forecast mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) target <8% rolling 12 months.
  - Procurement cycle time target: PO issuance within 5 business days for standard vendors.

6) Templates and examples (appendices)
- Contract checklist (CSV headings): counterparty, contract_type, effective_date, term_months, auto_renew, revenue_account, owner, legal_status.
- Example PO approval YAML snippet:
  approvers:
    - level: manager
      threshold: 10000
    - level: director
      threshold: 100000
    - level: vp_finance
      threshold: 1000000
- Sample revenue schedule table (text):
  | Invoice Date | Contract | Amount | Deferred | Recognized This Period | GL Account |
  |-------------|----------|--------|----------|-----------------------|------------|
  | 2026-01-01  | ORD-123  | $120,000 | $90,000 | $10,000 | 4001     |

Change management & updates:
- This playbook is reviewed annually or when material accounting or procurement policy changes occur. Amendments must be approved by VP Finance and GC.
